I will think out loud first, then write down my plan.

My land is 13.1 mu. I always grow wheat then maize on the same ground — that is how we do it here. I keep about 10 mu for the wheat-maize rotation. The other 3.1 mu I plant cotton, like I have done for many years. My wife and I still work the land; two of our children go out for work, but they come back at harvest if I call them.

**Wheat (10 mu, winter):**
Last year I got maybe 450 kg per mu, not bad. I will do the same. Before planting in October I plough once and put down one bag of compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind, per mu — that is 50 jin, no wait, 50 kg, one sack. Then in spring when the wheat turns green I spread one bag of urea per mu, 50 kg, together with the first irrigation. I water 4 times — before winter, then green-up, then jointing, then filling. The fertilizer dealer in town sells me the same brand every year, I trust him. For pests I spray twice — once for aphids in spring, once for the rust if I see it on the leaves. Seeds I buy the improved kind from the agro-shop, "Jimai" something, I forget the number but the dealer knows.

**Maize (10 mu, summer):**
After wheat I do not plough, I just drill the maize seed straight into the stubble — everyone does this now, saves a lot of work and diesel. I buy hybrid seed, the Zhengdan or Xianyu kind, whatever the shop has. One bag of compound per mu at sowing, then when the maize is knee-high I topdress half a bag of urea per mu. I irrigate 2 times if the rain is poor — once at the big trumpet stage, once at tasseling. Spray once for the corn borer, maybe twice if I see worms. Last year around 550 kg per mu.

**Cotton (3.1 mu, spring):**
Cotton is more trouble but the price is decent. I plough in spring, put one bag compound plus half a bag of urea per mu before planting, then topdress again when flowers come. Cotton needs a lot of spraying — aphids, bollworm, mirid bug — I go through the field maybe 5-6 times with the sprayer. I water 3 times from the well. I pick about 260 kg of seed cotton per mu usually.

I keep my costs tight. I do not buy more fertilizer than my neighbors use — if they get good harvest with that much, I do the same.
